deep.reconstruction:
The page contains two independent computations. Each is a closedness or integrability condition for a 1-form in two variables.

(I) Variables z,u. Unknowns φ, ψ, χ, f are functions of (z,u). Define A = φ f_z + ψ f and B = φ f_u + χ f. Riemann computes the 'curl' of the form A dz + B du. Expanding, the φ f_{zu} terms cancel, giving
A_u − B_z = (φ_u − χ) f_z + (ψ − φ_z) f_u + (ψ_u − χ_z) f.
He first tried to rewrite this as p f_z + q f_u + (p_z + q_u) f and struck the attempt out, since it is wrong.
He then introduced p, q so that the φ-part becomes a pure derivative. The definitions are implicit; making them explicit is mine: p = ψ − φ_z and q = χ − φ_u. Then
A = ∂(φ f)/∂z + p f,
B = ∂(φ f)/∂u + q f,
and since ∂²(φf)/∂u∂z cancels,
A_u − B_z = ∂(p f)/∂u − ∂(q f)/∂z.
This means that the 'φ-part' of a linear first-order expression in f contributes nothing to the curl; only the zero-order coefficients p, q matter. This is a Lagrange/Green-type identity of the kind used in adjoint-operator arguments. The page itself gives no indication of the intended application.

(II) Variables x,y,z. Consider the surface f(x,y,z)=0, with x regarded as a function of (y,z), so x_y = −f_y/f_x and x_z = −f_z/f_x. Riemann takes the 1-form (φ dy + ψ dz)/f_x on the surface; this is the kind of form appearing in the theory of integrals on algebraic surfaces / residue forms dy/f_x. He writes its closedness condition
d/dz (φ/f_x) = d/dy (ψ/f_x),
where the derivatives are total derivatives along the surface: d/dz g = g_z − g_x f_z/f_x.
An intermediate fragment, −φ_x f_z/(f_x f_x), is one of the terms of d/dz(φ/f_x). Multiplying through by f_x², he obtains
−φ_x f_z + φ_z f_x − φ f_{xz} + φ f_{xx} f_z/f_x = −ψ_x f_y + ψ_y f_x − ψ f_{xy} + ψ f_{xx} f_y/f_x.
errors: The struck line '= p f_z + q f_u + (p_z+q_u) f' is incorrect. With p = ψ−φ_z and q = χ−φ_u, the correct form is p f_u − q f_z + (p_u − q_z) f. Riemann deleted the line himself.

In the first bracket the χ appears struck through, but the correct coefficient of f_z is (φ_u − χ). Either the strike removed a mistaken '∂χ' and only the χ should remain, or the strike itself is a slip. The intended result requires −χ.
No other errors: the identity A_u−B_z = (pf)_u − (qf)_z and both sides of the surface closedness condition (after multiplying by f_x²) check out.

results.what: Rewriting the curl of A dz + B du, with A,B linear first-order in f, so that the φ-terms drop out: A_u − B_z = (pf)_u − (qf)_z
results.modern_name: Lagrange/Green identity (divergence form of a bilinear differential expression; adjoint operator)
results.usually_credited_to: Lagrange (adjoint), Green; in the 2D hyperbolic setting Riemann 1860

results.what: Closedness condition for the 1-form (φ dy + ψ dz)/f_x on the surface f=0, computed by implicit differentiation
results.modern_name: Closedness of a differential form on an implicitly defined surface (precursor of Picard-type integrals / Poincaré residue forms)
results.usually_credited_to: Classical (Euler/Jacobi implicit differentiation); integrals on algebraic surfaces: Picard, Noether (1880s)

deep.surprise_reason: Both computations are routine calculus identities: a divergence-form rewriting and an exactness condition on an implicit surface. The second hints at an interest in integrals on algebraic surfaces, but nothing beyond the elementary check is carried out.

checkable.sympy: z,u=symbols('z u'); phi,psi,chi,f=[Function(n)(z,u) for n in ['phi','psi','chi','f']]; A=phi*diff(f,z)+psi*f; B=phi*diff(f,u)+chi*f; simplify(diff(A,u)-diff(B,z)-((diff(phi,u)-chi)*diff(f,z)+(psi-diff(phi,z))*diff(f,u)+(diff(psi,u)-diff(chi,z))*f))==0
p=psi-diff(phi,z); q=chi-diff(phi,u); simplify(A-(diff(phi*f,z)+p*f))==0 and simplify(B-(diff(phi*f,u)+q*f))==0 and simplify(diff(A,u)-diff(B,z)-(diff(p*f,u)-diff(q*f,z)))==0
checkable.asserts: With p=ψ−φ_z, q=χ−φ_u: A=(φf)_z+pf, B=(φf)_u+qf, and A_u−B_z=(pf)_u−(qf)_z

checkable.sympy: x,y,z=symbols('x y z'); f,phi=Function('f')(x,y,z),Function('phi')(x,y,z); g=phi/diff(f,x); Dz=lambda h: diff(h,z)-diff(h,x)*diff(f,z)/diff(f,x); simplify(Dz(g)*diff(f,x)**2-(-diff(phi,x)*diff(f,z)+diff(phi,z)*diff(f,x)-phi*diff(f,x,z)+phi*diff(f,x,2)*diff(f,z)/diff(f,x)))==0
checkable.asserts: f_x² · d/dz(φ/f_x) along f=0 equals the left side written by Riemann
f_x² · d/dy(ψ/f_x) along f=0 equals the right side written by Riemann

transcription_corrections: First bracket: the image reads (∂φ/∂u − χ) with an apparent strike over the χ-symbol. The mathematically required term is −χ, not a deleted term.
In the φ-line, the term '−∂²f/∂x∂z φ[?]' is written as '−(∂²f/∂x∂z + (∂²f/∂x²)(∂f/∂z)/(∂f/∂x)) φ'. The trailing φ multiplies both terms, so the '[?]' is unnecessary.
The struck symbol before (φ dy + ψ dz)/(∂f/∂x) is an illegible deleted label. The struck 'pf' before ∂A/∂u − ∂B/∂z is correctly marked as deleted.
In the expression ∂(ψ/f_x)/∂y the numerator was overwritten (an 'f' over ψ); the intended reading ∂(ψ/f_x)/∂y is confirmed by the following lines.
